extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants/owners, patent practitioners, and patent examiners (US PTO)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules for calculating patent term extensions (human drugs, animal drugs, veterinary biologicals), issuance and termination of extension certificates/orders, interim extensions, and detailed requirements for deposit of biological material (including sequence disclosures) for U.S. patent applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation of patent term extension for an animal drug product (§ 1.778)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a § 1.750 determination finds a patent for an animal drug eligible, the term is extended by the time (in days) calculated under this section; the extension runs from the original patent expiration (or earlier terminal-disclaimer date).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Length of regulatory review period is determined by HHS and is the sum of: (1) days from the earlier of initiation of a major health/environmental effects test or effectiveness of a subsection (j) exemption to the date an application was initially submitted under section 512; and (2) days from initial submission under subsection (b) of section 512 to approval. The extended term is the regulatory review period reduced as appropriate by: (d)(1)(i) days in (c)(1) and (c)(2) that were on or before the patent issue date; (d)(1)(ii) days during which HHS determines applicant lacked due diligence under 35 U.S.C.156(d)(2)(B); and (d)(1)(iii) one-half the remaining days in (c)(1) after those reductions (ignore half-days). Then: add that number to the original term (shortened by terminal disclaimer) (d)(2); add 14 years to approval date (d)(3); compare ends from (d)(2) and (d)(3) and select earlier (d)(4). If patent issued after Nov 16, 1988, also consider adding 5 years to original expiration and select earlier between that and the earlier of (d)(4) (d)(5). If issued before Nov 16, 1988, there are special rules depending on whether tests/exemptions were begun/submitted before Nov 16, 1988 (add 5 years or add 3 years and compare).

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation of patent term extension for a veterinary biological product (§ 1.779)
rubrics_metrics.description: If § 1.750 finds a patent for a veterinary biological product eligible, extend the term by days calculated under this section; extension runs from original expiration or earlier terminal-disclaimer date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory review period (determined by Secretary of Agriculture) is the sum of: (1) days from date authority to prepare an experimental biological product under the Virus-Serum-Toxin Act became effective to date a license application was submitted; and (2) days from initial submission of license application to date license was issued. Extended term is the regulatory review period reduced by: (d)(1)(i) days in (c)(1) and (c)(2) that were on or before patent issue date; (d)(1)(ii) days during which Secretary determines applicant lacked due diligence under 35 U.S.C.156(d)(2)(B); (d)(1)(iii) one-half remaining days in (c)(1) after reductions (ignore half-days). Then add reduced days to original term shortened by any terminal disclaimer (d)(2); add 14 years to license issuance date (d)(3); compare dates from (d)(2) and (d)(3) and select earlier (d)(4). Special rules apply if patent issued after Nov 16, 1988 (add 5 years then compare) or before Nov 16, 1988 depending on whether a request/authority was submitted before that date (add 5 or 3 years and compare).

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation of patent term extension for drugs (human): selection and reductions (cross-referenced)
rubrics_metrics.description: General method used in analogous human drug/product sections: compute regulatory review period, subtract portions as specified (on-or-before issue date, due-diligence lapses, half of certain periods), add reduced period to patent term or add statutory fixed-year anchors, then compare candidate expiration dates and select the earliest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the chunk includes animal/veterinary specific formulas, the underlying rubric: (1) determine regulatory review period per statute; (2) subtract days on/before patent issue date and days where due diligence lacking per 35 U.S.C.156(d)(2)(B); (3) subtract half the remaining in certain pre-submission periods; (4) add reduced days to patent term (shortened by terminal disclaimer) and/or add statutory fixed years to approval/issuance dates; (5) compare resulting dates and select the earlier. This pattern repeats across product types with statute-specific dates and fixed-year additions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate or order of extension issuance (§ 1.780)
rubrics_metrics.description: If § 1.750 determines a patent eligible and to be extended, the Office will issue a sealed certificate of extension or an order granting interim extension under 35 U.S.C.156(d)(5); such certificate/order is recorded in the patent file and considered part of the original patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Issuance is published in the Official Gazette. Orders granting interim extensions (including identity of product under review) are published in Official Gazette and Federal Register. No certificate/order will be issued if the term cannot be extended even if eligible — the final §1.750 determination will indicate that no certificate/order will issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Only one patent extended per regulatory review period; priority among multiple applications (§ 1.785(a)-(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Only one patent may be extended for a regulatory review period for any product. If multiple applications for the same patent are filed, certificate of extension is based on the first-filed application for extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a single applicant files to extend multiple patents based on the same regulatory review period, absent an election the certificate issues for the patent with the earliest issuance date among those patents. If an application seeks extension of a patent based on the same regulatory review period relied on in other applications, the certificate will issue only if the patent owner or agent is the holder of the regulatory approval for that period. Applications are considered complete/formal regardless of identification of the regulatory approval holder; Office may request such information when multiple applications are received, with a non-extendable response period ≥ one month; failure to provide info is conclusive that applicant is not approval holder. Determinations under this section are included in final §1.750 notice of eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim extension application requirements (§ 1.790)
rubrics_metrics.description: An owner of record (or agent) who reasonably expects the regulatory review period to extend beyond patent expiration may submit one or more interim extension applications for up to one year each, not exceeding the maximum statutory extension under 35 U.S.C.156(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications for interim extension must be filed via USPTO patent electronic filing system per USPTO requirements. Complete initial interim applications must be filed 6 months to 15 days before patent expiration, include a statement that it's timely and identify last possible filing date, and include all information required for formal application under §1.740 and complete application under §1.741 except: (i) read certain §1.740/1.741 paragraphs in context of product under regulatory review; (ii) some paragraphs not applicable (a)(3) and (5) of §1.740). Must include statement that applicable regulatory review period has begun. Subsequent interim applications must be filed between 60 and 30 days before expiration of preceding interim extension, may be limited in content to a request plus any missing required materials, and must state that regulatory review period has not been completed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination of interim extension upon product approval (§ 1.791)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any interim extension granted under 35 U.S.C.156(d)(5) terminates at the end of the 60-day period beginning on the date the product receives permission for commercial marketing or use, unless an application for full extension under §§1.740/1.741 (including any additional statutory information) is filed within that 60-day period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the patent owner/agent files a complete extension application within the 60-day period, the patent shall be further extended in accordance with 35 U.S.C.156.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of biological material for deposit purposes (§ 1.801)
rubrics_metrics.description: Biological material includes material capable of self-replication directly or indirectly (examples: bacteria, fungi/yeast, algae, protozoa, eukaryotic cells, cell lines, hybridomas, plasmids, viruses, plant tissue cells, lichens, seeds). Non-living materials reproducible from a living cell (viruses, vectors, organelles) may be deposited via host cell deposit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This definition frames what materials are subject to deposit rules for patent purposes under 35 U.S.C.101-related regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need or opportunity to make a deposit (§ 1.802)
rubrics_metrics.description: Biological material may be referenced or deposited when an invention is or relies on such material, but deposit is not required unless access is necessary to satisfy the statutory requirements of 35 U.S.C.112.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deposits are unnecessary if material is known and readily available to the public or can be made/isolated without undue experimentation. Once deposited in a compliant depository, material is considered readily available even if access is legally restricted for safety/public health. Reference to or deposit of material does not create a presumption that deposit was necessary to satisfy 35 U.S.C.112.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable depository criteria and recognition process (§ 1.803)
rubrics_metrics.description: A deposit is recognized for patent purposes if made in (1) an International Depositary Authority under the Budapest Treaty, or (2) any other depository the Office recognizes as suitable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suitability is determined by the Director based on administrative/technical competence and agreement to comply with deposit terms; Director may consult impartial experts. Required depository attributes: continuous existence; independence from depositor control; adequate staff/facilities to examine viability and store uncontaminated; sufficient safety measures; impartiality/objectivity; ability to furnish samples expeditiously; prompt notice to depositors if unable to furnish samples with reasons. A depository seeking recognition must submit detailed info (name/address, legal status, scientific standing, staff/facilities, intent to be available to any depositor under same conditions, kinds of material accepted, fees). Recognition status changes are published in the Office Gazette.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of making an original deposit (§ 1.804)
rubrics_metrics.description: An original deposit identified in a patent application may be made any time before filing the application or, subject to §1.809, during pendency of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the deposit is made after the effective filing date, the applicant must promptly submit a corroborating statement from someone able to confirm the deposited material is that specifically identified in the filed application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replacement or supplemental deposit rules and certificate of correction requirements (§ 1.805)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the depository cannot furnish samples or the deposit is contaminated or lost capability, the depositor must notify the Office. Replacement/supplemental deposits during pendency are governed by original deposit need rules; replacement/supplemental deposits require meeting original deposit requirements and (for patents) must be accompanied by a certificate of correction meeting specific terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certificate of correction must identify accession number, deposit date, and depository name/address, be requested promptly after replacement/supplemental deposit, include reason for replacement/supplement, include corroborating statement that replacement is identical to original, show that patent owner acted diligently in making replacement/supplement, include a statement that the term of replacement/supplement expires no earlier than the original deposit term, and otherwise establish regulatory compliance. Failure to replace or to timely request proper certificate of correction after notice that depository can't furnish samples will cause the application/patent to be treated as if no deposit were made. If deposit is replaced per rules, Office will apply a rebuttable presumption of identity between original and replacement deposits in Office proceedings. Replacement/supplement during pendency may be made for any reason, but if a depository could furnish samples, Office will not recognize a replacement deposit made by a patent owner in Office proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Term of deposit (§ 1.806)
rubrics_metrics.description: Deposits made before or during pendency must be for at least 30 years and at least 5 years after the most recent request for a sample; samples must be stored under agreements making them available beyond the enforceable life of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minimum durations ensure availability throughout and beyond patent enforceable term.

rubrics_metrics.name: Viability requirement and viability statements (§ 1.807)
rubrics_metrics.description: Deposits capable of self-replication must be viable at time of deposit and during deposit term; viability may be tested by the depository and test need only show capability to reproduce.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For deposits not made under the Budapest Treaty, a viability statement must be filed in the application containing: depository name/address; depositor name/address; date of deposit; identity and accession number; date of viability test; procedures used to obtain sample if test not by depository; and a statement that deposit is capable of reproduction. If viability test indicates non-viability on receipt or examiner cannot accept applicant's viability statement for valid scientific reasons, examiner proceeds as if no deposit was made. Examiner will accept viability conclusion from a recognized depository under §1.803(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Furnishing of samples (§ 1.808)
rubrics_metrics.description: Deposits must be made under conditions assuring access during pendency to parties entitled under §1.14 and 35 U.S.C.122, and that all depositor-imposed restrictions on public availability will be irrevocably removed upon patent grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depositor may contract to require sample requests (during patent term) be: in writing/tangible form and dated; contain requester name/address and accession number; and be communicated by depository to depositor along with date sample furnished and name/address of recipient. The Office will certify whether a deposit was made under conditions that make it publicly available as of patent issue date upon request containing depository name/address, accession number, patent number/issue date referring to deposit, and requestor name/address.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination procedures regarding deposits (§ 1.809)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners must determine under §1.104 if a deposit is needed, and if needed, whether a deposit made is acceptable; if needed and not made/replaced/supplemented per regulations, examiner shall reject affected claims under 35 U.S.C.112 explaining need for deposit or why deposit is unacceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant/patent owner must reply by (1) making acceptable original/replacement/supplemental deposit or assuring Office in writing that acceptable deposit will be made (or patent owner requesting certificate of correction meeting §1.805(b),(c)); or (2) arguing why deposit is not needed and/or why deposit made should be accepted. Other replies are nonresponsive. Rejection will repeat until cured or examiner convinced deposit not needed. If application otherwise allowable except for needed deposit and Office has written assurance that acceptable deposit will be made, Office may issue notice of allowability and set a three-month non-extendable period to make the deposit to avoid abandonment. For each deposit, the specification must contain accession number, deposit date, description sufficient to identify the material and permit examination, and depository name/address. Amendments to add accession number, deposit date, or depository name/address must be filed before or with payment of the issue fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nucleotide and/or amino acid sequence disclosure scope (§ 1.821)
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications filed prior to July 1, 2022, nucleotide/amino acid sequence rules apply to unbranched sequences of 4+ amino acids or 10+ nucleotides; branched sequences and sequences shorter than those thresholds are excluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ‘Specifically defined’ excludes Xaa (for amino acids) and 'n' (for nucleotides) as placeholders. Nucleotides limited to symbols in Appendix A; certain modifications may be described per Appendix B but not shown explicitly in the sequence. Amino acids are L-amino acids listed in Appendix C; sequences with D-amino acids are excluded. Post-translational modifications may be described in Feature section with modifications noted per Appendix D but not shown explicitly. Peptides/proteins expressible using Appendix C symbols together with Feature descriptions of modifications (linkages, cross-links, non-peptidyl bonds, end caps) are embraced by the definition.
